about: What a failed turn says in both CLIs, the chat and -p alike (2026-09-25): a headline in plain words and one line of what to do, never the platform's protocol text. `message` is what the SDK raised or streamed (each SDK words the same refusal differently: the TypeScript proxy skill keeps the socket's close code, the Python one rewrites a refused sign-in and its error keeps the cause). `code` is the stable code `-p --output-format stream-json` reports for Robutler's own refusals (null: the SDK's own code, if any, is passed through). `proxy` is true when the turn ran on Robutler's models; `proxy_url` is then the socket the chat used. `model` (2026-09-27), when given, is the model the turn ran on: a key hint names ITS provider's variable, and OPENAI_API_KEY when the model names no provider this SDK has a client for. Robutler's own credit refusals that say what a call needs reserved or what unfinished calls hold (the cli-billing cases, 2026-09-27) keep Robutler's sentence: the first sentence is the headline, the rest the hint, and `credits_held` is their code when credits are held. Python: tests/cli/test_failure_presentation.py, TypeScript: tests/unit/cli/failures.test.ts.
